messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
In a simple projectile‑motion picture (ignoring air resistance, friction, etc.) the horizontal distance travelled after a time \(t\) is just the horizontal component of the velocity multiplied by the elapsed time:

\[
x(t)=v\,\cos(\theta)\;t .
\]

So if you know the launch speed \(v\), the launch angle \(\theta\) (in radians or degrees as long as you convert appropriately), and the time \(t\), plug them into that formula to get the range.

If you’d like to see this expressed in code, you could call the helper function like this (assuming you supply numeric values):

```python
from functions import calculate_projectile_range

# Example:
distance = calculate_projectile_range(
    initial_velocity=v,
    angle=theta,   # in degrees
    time=t
)
```

That function internally does exactly the same thing—computes \(v \cos(\theta) t\)—and returns the result.
